experiments.revision_reason: Transport correction only; the four cases, their assertions and their parameters are unchanged. The previous run's new case failed with its own operands showing the artefact: event `default_capacity_parked_cluster` recorded nodes_parked 1, decided_before 1030 = decided_after 1030, although only one node had parked, so a quorum (the healthy leader plus the other live follower) was still available - progress had stopped because each sender's forwarding task was blocked awaiting delivery into the parked node's full incoming channel, which also stalls that sender's unrelated traffic. Delivery is now per destination: senders only push into the destination's queue and one task per destination awaits handle_incoming, so a parked destination accumulates messages in its own queue and cannot block anyone else. The same correction removes that confound from the cluster-level case in the same harness. Locally all four cases pass with the corrected transport (11.5s), with the default-capacity case reporting event_capacity 1024, nodes_parked 2, decided_before = decided_after = 1119 and append_notify_timeout_reached true.

The new case is the scope control for the windowed finding: node 1 accepts its own entry at index 1 while *both* followers' receipts are dropped, so node 1 stays at decided 0 with its call pending although a quorum accepted the entry; node 2 then takes over, adopts the followers' log (which contains node 1's entry), decides index 1, and node 1 re-synchronizes. The expectation from the adoption path (prepare-phase Promise log_sync / take_max_promise_sync) is that Ok(1) is then truthful, i.e. the entry at index 1 is node 1's own. implementation.instructions: Write Rust #[test] integration tests using the captured crate's public API and existing dependencies. The controller fixes the workspace lock and tools; build reuse is specific to a manifest, integration test target and saved build basis. Switching crates may require a first heavy dependency build. Consult research.json build_inputs for preparation evidence and current seed availability; unlisted targets are not known to be prepared, and available seeds still require execution-time validation. Only the generated test target runs, serially with --nocapture and --locked --offline. Optional test_names selects exact full test names; omission runs the whole generated target. Unselected code still compiles. Emit complete CA_EVENT JSON lines. Helpers are workspace-relative; never replace manifests, locks, build scripts or Cargo configuration. No extra feature flags are added; original dev-dependencies can enable additional features. Actual compiler-artifact records describe reuse; declaration syntax does not establish active cfg branches or private-state reachability.
